anchor.quote: Write $b = \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ for the rounded-up base-2 logarithm of $n$.
Write $p = 6b$ for the working precision, the parameter that sets the coefficient width up to a constant factor
Write $T$ for the power of two that sets the number of cells in the padded box
Write $V = Tp$ for the logical bit volume of the padded box
The exponent $\epsilon$ is a fixed positive rational number.
The exponent $c$ is a fixed positive rational number.
The exponent $\tau$ is a fixed rational number between zero and one.
The exponent $\lambda'$ is a fixed rational number below one.
The exponent $\delta$ is a fixed rational number
The factor $\alpha = \Theta(p^{1/4+\epsilon/2})$ is the factor in the cost of the Gaussian line maps.
Write $d$ for the number of axes of the padded box
Write $K = \lfloor d^{c} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ for the width of the address chunks, in bits.
Write $r$ for the largest axis length of the padded box, a power of two.
Write $\ell = \log_2 r = \Theta(p^{1-\epsilon})$ for its base-2 logarithm.

gaps.quote: Prefix-slot moves and individual butterfly rounds
gaps.note: The table names prefix-slot moves as a cost operation, but the page neither explains the term nor links to a page for it.
Butterfly rounds, individual and simultaneous, are cost units that the page never explains or links.
The page does not say what a transform layout is, so the reader cannot tell what the chunk exchanges cost.
CRT (the Chinese remainder theorem or its map) is not explained or linked on this page.

gaps.quote: the factor in the cost of the Gaussian line maps
gaps.note: Gaussian line maps are the source of the factor alpha and of a table row, but the page does not explain them or link a page for them.
Chirps and twists are named as cost items without any explanation or link.
The word packed is not explained, and the page does not say what a packed polynomial product computes.

gaps.quote: for the logical bit volume of the padded box
gaps.note: The formula V = Tp is given, but the page does not say what makes the volume logical, so the reader cannot tell what V counts.

gaps.quote: Write $\ell = \log_2 r = \Theta(p^{1-\epsilon})$ for its base-2 logarithm.
gaps.note: r is defined only as the largest axis length. The page never says how the d axes and the T cells are related, so the reader cannot check that log r is Theta(p^(1-epsilon)). Every later exponent that uses ell depends on this step.

The table gives a logarithm as the cost and lists power 1-epsilon, but the page does not show that log(rp) is at most a constant times p^(1-epsilon), which needs the unproved value of ell and a comparison of log p with it.
A power p^delta is a constant only if delta is at most zero, and the page says only that delta is a fixed rational number. The page does not show that the final scaling term is bounded by a constant.

gaps.quote: The parameters are chosen so that every term fits the bound
gaps.note: The page asserts that the parameters fit the bound but gives no values or constraints on epsilon, c, tau, lambda', delta, so the reader cannot check that any choice makes every power below one.

The colon introduces no computation. The page never lists the margins of the table rows, never shows that the smallest is exactly 2kappa, and never shows that each power is at most 1-kappa, which the next sentence about a constant times p^(1-kappa) assumes.
